title: The Bantu expansion changed Africa. Scientists are still tracing how.
gist: A Knowable Magazine feature reviews how linguists, archaeologists and geneticists are reconstructing the Bantu expansion, a migration from the Cameroon Grassfields beginning 6,000-4,000 years ago that spread farming, iron-working and ~500 languages now spoken by ~350 million Africans. Evidence now suggests groups crossed the Congo rainforest together before splitting, though funding and data gaps persist.

themes.theme: Scale and origins of the Bantu expansion

insights.claim: Around 350 million Africans today speak one of roughly 500 distinct Bantu languages, the result of a migration beginning 6,000 to 4,000 years ago from western Africa.
insights.speaker: Knowable Magazine
insights.so_what: Demographic and linguistic backdrop for much of sub-Saharan Africa.
insights.quote: around 350 million Africans speak one of roughly 500 distinct Bantu tongues

insights.claim: Linguistic and genetic data point to the Grassfields region of Cameroon as the Bantu homeland, though conclusive archaeological proof is thin.
insights.speaker: Knowable Magazine

insights.claim: A 2024 analysis of 1,763 African genomes found the greatest Bantu genetic diversity in western Africa, declining with distance, a typical signature of population expansion.
insights.speaker: Knowable Magazine
insights.so_what: Genomic methods resolved the migration-vs-cultural-diffusion debate.
insights.quote: This is a typical signature of a population expanding from one place to another

insights.claim: Bantu speakers' sedentary farming lifestyle and iron tools let them produce more food and grow in number, propelling expansion and displacing or marginalizing hunter-gatherer groups.
insights.speaker: Knowable Magazine
insights.so_what: Classic example of technology-driven demographic expansion.

insights.claim: Evidence now suggests Bantu groups crossed the Congo rainforest together and split into eastern and southern streams only at its southern fringe roughly 2,500 to 3,500 years ago.

insights.so_what: Revision of the earlier split-before-rainforest model.

insights.claim: By 1100 to 1600 AD, Bantu state societies traded across the Indian Ocean, importing Chinese porcelain and glass beads and exporting gold, ivory and iron, with southern African iron reputed superior to India's.
insights.speaker: Knowable Magazine
insights.so_what: Historic evidence of African participation in long-distance trade networks.

insights.claim: Great Zimbabwe smelters used natural-draft furnaces requiring no bellows and added bone, whose calcium accelerates iron separation, possibly as ritual with technical benefit.
